title: Spoken Language Understanding
header: Wednesday 30 September 2026 - 16:30-18:30 - Area 11 - Poster 1 - Spoken Language Understanding

items.title: DEBATE: A Dataset for Disentangling Textual Ambiguity in Mandarin Through Speech
items.authors: Haotian Guo(Hunan University); Jing Han(Hunan University; Yuelushan Center for Industrial Innovation); Yongfeng Tu(Malanshan Audio & Video Laboratory); Shihao Gao(Hunan University); Weihao Gan(Malanshan Audio & Video Laboratory); Zixing Zhang(Hunan University)
items.abstract: Despite extensive research on textual and visual disambiguation, disambiguation through speech (DTS) remains underexplored. This is largely due to the lack of high-quality datasets that pair spoken sentences with richly ambiguous text. To address this gap, we present DEBATE, a unique public Chinese speech-text dataset designed to study how speech cues and patterns such as pronunciation, pauses, stress, and intonation can help resolve textual ambiguity and reveal a speaker's true intent. DEBATE contains 1,001 carefully selected ambiguous utterances, each recorded by 10 native speakers to capture diverse spoken disambiguations. We detail the rigorous data pipeline and benchmark threelarge speech language models, revealing a significant gap between machine and human intent understanding. DEBATE represents the first effort of its kind and offers a foundation for building similar DTS datasets across languages and cultures.

items.title: Distilling Structured Reasoning into SpeechLLMs for Spoken Language Understanding
items.authors: Toshihiro Tsukagoshi(Shizuoka University); Natsuo Yamashita(Hitachi, Ltd.); Kota Dohi(Hitachi, Ltd.); Hiroaki Kokubo(Hitachi, Ltd.); Masaaki Yamamoto(Hitachi, Ltd.)
items.abstract: Recent Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs) have emerged as a promising approach for end-to-end Spoken Language Understanding (SLU). While adapting SpeechLLMs to specific SLU tasks such as intent classification requires alignment with task-specific label schemas, conventional fine-tuning still struggles to separate semantically adjacent intent categories. To address this, we propose Reasoning-Guided Fine-Tuning (RG-FT), which distills structured reasoning trajectories generated by DeepSeek-R1, comprising candidate enumeration, rejection reasoning, and label prediction, into SpeechLLMs as a multitask objective. Explicitly verbalizing why incorrect candidates are rejected forces the model to capture fine-grained distinctions and sharpen inter-class decision boundaries. At inference, only direct label prediction is used, incurring zero additional computational cost. Experiments on multiple SLU benchmarks and six SpeechLLMs demonstrate that RG-FT consistently improves SLU performance.

items.title: Enhancing Audio Reasoning via Semantic Summary Prediction
items.authors: Francesco Bonzi(Concordia University; Mila - Quebec AI Institute); Pooneh Mousavi(Concordia University; Mila - Quebec AI Institute); Cem Subakan(Université Laval; Mila - Quebec AI Institute); Mirco Ravanelli(Concordia University; Mila - Quebec AI Institute)
items.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) perform well on complex question answering but often show a reasoning gap, where explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reduces accuracy compared to direct answers. We hypothesize that long reasoning sequences shift attention away from the audio input. To address this, we propose SPARE (Semantic Prediction for Audio REasoning), which introduces a register token aligned with the final conclusion using a cosine similarity loss with a Sentence-BERT embedding. This conditions the model's latent space with the target semantic goal before reasoning begins. Experiments on MMAU and MMAR with SALMONN show improved zero-shot reasoning and stronger early attention to audio without additional inference cost.

items.title: Incremental End-to-End Spoken Dialogue State Tracking with a Multimodal LLM and Reinforcement Learning
items.authors: Tomoya Higuchi(The University of Electro-Communications); Michimasa Inaba(The University of Electro-Communications)
items.abstract: End-to-end spoken dialogue state tracking (DST) infers belief states directly from speech, avoiding cascading errors in ASR-DST pipelines. This paper proposes an incremental DST method using a multimodal large language model (Qwen2.5-Omni-7B) that generates transcripts and symbolic state updates from raw audio. Unlike conventional approaches that regenerate the full state each turn, our method predicts only symbolic edit operations relative to the previous state, reducing output length and the risk of corrupting unchanged slots. We apply a two-stage training recipe: supervised fine-tuning followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which directly optimizes generation-level rewards for transcript accuracy, DST correctness, and format validity. Experiments on SpokenWOZ demonstrate that incremental updates substantially outperform full-state prediction, and GRPO further improves accuracy, achieving the best reported results on this benchmark.

items.title: Joint Speech And Text Training For LLM-based End-To-End Spoken Dialogue State Tracking
items.authors: Katia Vendrame(Brno University of Technology); Bolaji Yusuf(Brno University of Technology); Santosh Kesiraju(Brno University of Technology); Šimon Sedláček(Brno University of Technology); Oldřich Plchot(Brno University of Technology); Honza Černocký(Brno University of Technology)
items.abstract: End-to-end spoken dialogue state tracking (DST) is made difficult by having to handle speech input with scarce training data. Combining speech foundation encoders and large language models has emerged as an approach to alleviate this difficulty. Although this approach results in strong spoken DST models, achieving state-of-the-art performance in realistic multi-turn DST, it struggles to generalize across domains and requires annotated spoken DST training data for each domain of interest. However, collecting such data for every target domain is both costly and difficult. Noting that textual DST data is more easily obtained for various domains, in this work, we propose jointly training on available spoken DST data and written textual data from other domains as a way to achieve cross-domain generalization. We conduct experiments which show the efficacy of our proposed method for getting good cross-domain DST performance without relying on spoken training data from the target domains.

items.title: MAC-SLU: Multi-Intent Automotive Cabin Spoken Language Understanding Benchmark
items.authors: Yuezhang Peng(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Chonghao Cai(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Ziang Liu(Central South University); Shuai Fan(AISpeech Co., Ltd.); Sheng Jiang(AISpeech Co., Ltd.); Hua Xu(AISpeech Co., Ltd.); Yuxin Liu(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Sheng Wang(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Qiguang Chen(Harbin Institute of Technology); Yao Li(Shanghai Aviation Electric Co., Ltd.); Kele Xu(National University of Defense Technology); Kai Yu(Shanghai Jiao Tong University; AISpeech Co., Ltd.); Libo Qin(Harbin Institute of Technology); Xie Chen(Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Shanghai Innovation Institute)
items.abstract: Spoken Language Understanding (SLU), which aims to extract user semantics for downstream tasks, is vital to task-oriented dialog systems. Existing SLU datasets generally lack diversity and complexity, and a unified benchmark for the latest Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) remains absent. This work introduces MAC-SLU, a novel Multi-Intent Automotive Cabin Spoken Language Understanding Dataset, which increases task difficulty with authentic and complex multi-intent data. Based on MAC-SLU, we benchmarked leading LLMs and LALMs, covering methods like in-context learning (ICL), supervised fine-tuning (SFT), as well as end-to-end (E2E) and pipeline paradigms. Experiments show that while LLMs and LALMs have the potential to complete SLU tasks through ICL, their performance still lags significantly behind SFT. Meanwhile, E2E LALMs demonstrate performance comparable to pipeline approaches and effectively avoid error propagation from speech recognition.

items.title: MSU-Bench: Towards Understanding the Conversational Multi-Speaker Scenarios
items.authors: Zhaokai Sun(ASLP@NPU; SZ Loop Area Inst.; Li Auto); Shuai Wang(Nanjing Univ.; SZ Loop Area Inst.); Zhennan Lin(ASLP@NPU); Chengyou Wang(ASLP@NPU); Dehui Gao(ASLP@NPU); Yuang Cao(ASLP@NPU); Chunjiang He(ASLP@NPU); Pan Zhou(Li Auto); Lei Xie(ASLP@NPU)
items.abstract: Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) is moving from task-specific pipelines toward large audio language models (LALMs) that generate natural-language responses. However, existing speech benchmarks mainly focus on single-speaker settings or isolated subtasks, leaving speaker-centric understanding in realistic multi-speaker conversations insufficiently evaluated. We introduce MSU-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for multi-speaker conversational understanding, covering 16 speaker-centric tasks and 2,300 QA instances in a two-tier framework from speaker grounding to dialogue reasoning. We build a Gemini-assisted annotation and QA generation pipeline with human-in-the-loop verification, achieving high QA validity and strong agreement between human answers and verified labels. We further analyze speaker-referencing schemes and diagnostic error types to reveal bottlenecks in speaker grounding and reasoning. Experiments reveal clear gaps across model families, with closed-source systems leading overall but all models still facing challenges in complex speaker grounding and multi-speaker reasoning. The benchmark annotations, metadata, and evaluation scripts are available at the official GitHub repository: ASLP-lab/MSU-Bench.

items.title: MVCL-DAF++: Enhancing Multimodal Intent Recognition via Prototype-Aware Contrastive Alignment and Coarse-to-Fine Dynamic Attention Fusion
items.authors: Haofeng Huang(University of Shanghai for Science and Technology); Bin Li(CAS); Yifei Han(CAS); Long Zhang(CAS); Yangfan He(University of Minnesota-Twin Cities); Yaxin Xue(University of Leeds)
items.abstract: Multimodal intent recognition (MMIR) suffers from weak semantic grounding and poor robustness under noisy or rare-class conditions. We propose MVCL-DAF++, which extends MVCL-DAF with two key modules: (1) Prototype-aware contrastive alignment, aligning instances to class-level prototypes to enhance semantic consistency; and (2) Coarse-to-fine attention fusion, integrating global modality summaries with token-level features for hierarchical cross-modal interaction. On MIntRec and MIntRec2.0, MVCL-DAF++ achieves new state-of-the-art results, improving rare-class recognition by +1.05% and +4.18% WF1, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of prototype-guided learning and coarse-to-fine fusion for robust multimodal understanding.

items.title: PROGRESS: Coverage-guided RL to Train Search-augmented LLM Agent
items.authors: Sudipta Paul(Samsung Electronics); Vijay Srinivasan(Samsung Electronics); Vivek Kulkarni(Samsung Electronics); Aounon Kumar(Samsung Electronics); Yashas Malur Saidutta(Samsung Electronics); Wenbo Li(Samsung Electronics); Srinivas Chappidi(Samsung Electronics)
items.abstract: Existing search-augmented LLM agents are trained using Reinforcement Learning to boost its reasoning capabilities. However, these approaches primarily rely on outcome-level rewards which provide little supervision over search behavior and overlook agent's ability to decompose complex queries properly. To mitigate this issue, we propose PROGRESS which utilizes teacher-guided coverage reward to explicitly shape decomposed query generation of the policy model. During training, frozen teacher models are used to decompose complex queries into essential search queries. These essential search queries are utilized to guide the search behavior of the policy model. Integrated into an R1-style training framework, our approach provides lightweight guidance over query decomposition decisions without dense process-level supervision. Experiments show that coverage-guided RL improves overall task performance, highlighting the importance of explicitly supervising search strategies in agentic LLMs.

items.title: SFL-MTSC: Leveraging Semantic Frame-Level Multi-Task Self-Consistency for Robust Multi-Intent Spoken Language Understanding
items.authors: Po-Yen Chen(National Taiwan Normal University); Berlin Chen(National Taiwan Normal University)
items.abstract: Prompt-based spoken language understanding (SLU) with large language models (LLMs) often suffers from inconsistent intent-slot structures due to decoding stochasticity, particularly in multi-intent scenarios. In view of this, we propose Semantic Frame-Level Multi-Task Self-Consistency (SFL-MTSC), a novel structured aggregation framework operating at the semantic frame level. Instead of output-level majority voting, SFL-MTSC decomposes predictions into intent-specific frames, applies domain-intent grouping and slot-level clustering, and evaluates cluster reliability using path support scoring. Reliable frames are retained and re-integrated to form the final prediction. Zero-shot experiments on the MAC-SLU benchmark dataset show improved slot F1 and overall accuracy over single-path inference, while intent accuracy remains largely stable across most settings.

items.title: Selective Capability Unlearning in End-to-End Spoken Language Understanding
items.authors: Akanksha Singh(IISER Bhopal); Vinod Kumar Kurmi(IISER Bhopal)
items.abstract: Modern spoken language understanding (SLU) systems are increasingly deployed in real-world settings, where specific functionalities may need to be removed due to policy or safety constraints. In SLU, a functionality corresponds to an intent and its associated slot-generation behavior. However, in autoregressive models, suppressing a target intent does not eliminate the conditional mapping that generates slots conditioned on that intent. When the intent prefix is externally supplied, the model can reconstruct the original intent-slot structure. We identify this structural failure as capability persistence. We propose Binding Subspace (BSU), a representation-level framework that isolates and attenuates intent-conditioned directions underlying this mapping. Across SLU benchmarks, BSU substantially reduces forced-prefix recoverability while preserving retained performance.

items.title: GigaChat Audio: Time-aware Large Audio Language Model
items.authors: Aleksandr Kutsakov(SaluteDevices); Mariia Sadovina(SaluteDevices); Georgii Gospodinov(SaluteDevices); Alexandr Maximenko(SaluteDevices); Oleg Kutuzov(SaluteDevices); Pavel Bogomolov(SaluteDevices); Fyodor Minkin(SaluteDevices)
items.abstract: Temporal grounding in long recordings remains challenging for audio-conditioned LLMs. We present a time-aware audio LLM that answers questions with explicit timestamps over up to 120 minutes of input. Our approach interleaves periodic time markers with continuous audio tokens using large-scale synthetic supervision from a cascaded pipeline. Our model achieves strong temporal-grounding accuracy on short and long benchmarks and supports time-anchored fragment descriptions and summaries. Extensive ablations examine how time representation, marker frequency, tokenization, and duration-mixture design affect accuracy and computational cost. We release model weights and datasets to support further research on time-aware audio understanding, available at https://huggingface.co/ai-sage/GigaChat3.1-Audio-10B-A1.8B.
